title: Homotopy mapping property of enriched arrow inversion
statement:
Use small simplicial categories, their mapping simplicial sets, and their categories of path components as in [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting]. A Dwyer--Kan equivalence is a simplicial functor inducing weak homotopy equivalences on mapping sets and an equivalence of categories of path components. Give these categories the model structure with these weak equivalences, generating cofibrations $I$ and generating trivial cofibrations $J$ of that node, with acyclicity as in [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-cell-stability]. Write $h\mathrm{sCat}$ for its model homotopy category, computed using cofibrant-fibrant replacements and homotopy classes. Choose universes containing all categories displayed. For a small simplicial category $C$ and a set $W$ of vertex arrows, let $L_WC$ be the derived pushout of $C\leftarrow\coprod_W[1]\to\coprod_W\mathbb J$, where $[1]$ is the discrete walking arrow and $\mathbb J$ is the discrete two-object groupoid with exactly one arrow for each ordered pair of objects. Write $q:C\to L_WC$ for the structure map. For every small simplicial category $T$, restriction along $q$ is injective on homotopy classes,
$$q^*:\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(L_WC,T)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(C,T),$$
and its image consists precisely of the classes whose induced functor $\pi_0C\to\pi_0T$, taken up to natural isomorphism, sends every $w\in W$ to an isomorphism. This homotopy mapping property characterizes $(L_WC,q)$ up to isomorphism under $C$ in $h\mathrm{sCat}$. Enriched functors carrying a specified set of arrows into another induce maps of these localizations, compatible with composition in $h\mathrm{sCat}$.
